nodes.summary: Let $N \ge 4$ and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $1$. Then there are integers $q_1 \ge 2$ and $q_2 \ge 1$, with $q_2 = 1$ unless $q_1 = 3$, an integer $k \ge 2$ and integers $q_3, \dots, q_k \ge 1$ such that, with $B = q_1 + 2q_2 - 1$, $\lambda = (1^{q_1}, 2^{q_2}, B^{q_3}, (B(q_3+1))^{q_4}, \dots, (B(q_3+1) \cdots (q_{k-1}+1))^{q_k})$ (for $k = 2$ the only parts are $1$ and $2$). That…
nodes.title: Lee's form of double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: For an integer $B$, an integer $k \ge 2$ and integers $q_3, \dots, q_k \ge 1$, write $T_B(q_3, \dots, q_k)$ for the parts $B^{q_3}, (B(q_3+1))^{q_4}, \dots, (B(q_3+1) \cdots (q_{k-1}+1))^{q_k}$ (no parts when $k = 2$). Let $N \ge 4$ and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $1$. Then either $\lambda = (1^3, 2^{q_2}, T_{2(q_2+1)}(q_3, \dots, q_k))$ for some $q_2 > 1$, some $k \ge 2$ and some…
nodes.title: Lee's two forms of double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: Let $f(m)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $m$ into factors greater than $1$, with $f(0) = 0$ and $f(1) = 1$. For every $n \ge 4$, the number $d(n)$ of double-perfect partitions of $n$ of order $1$ is $f(n-1)$ unless $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, in which case $d(n) = f(n-1) - f((n-1)/4)$.
nodes.title: Lee's count of double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: Let $f(m)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $m$ into factors greater than $1$. Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 2(r+1)$ (equivalently $1 \le r \le \lfloor (N-2)/2 \rfloor$), put $M = 2(r+1)$, and let $u_r(N)$ be the number of double-perfect partitions of $N$ of order $r$. Then $u_r(N)$ equals $f(N-r) + (f(M) - 2f(r+1)) f((N-r)/(r+1)) - (f(M) - f(r+1)) f((N-r)/M)$ if $N \equiv r \pmod M$,…
nodes.title: Number of double-perfect partitions of higher order

nodes.summary: The partitions of $m$ contained in a partition $\lambda$ are the distinct sub-multisets of the parts of $\lambda$ with sum $m$. Let $v \ge 1$. There are a natural number $n$ and a partition $\lambda$ of $n$ that contains exactly $v$ partitions of some $m$ with $v \le m \le n - v$ and exactly one partition of every positive integer $m' < n$ other than $m$ if and only if $v = 1$ or $v = 2$.
nodes.title: Partitions with unique subsums except one

nodes.summary: For integers $a_1, \dots, a_k \ge 2$ write $P(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ for the perfect partition $(1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, (a_1a_2)^{a_3-1}, \dots, (a_1 \cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$. Let $N$ and $r \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $a_1, \dots, a_k \ge 2$ and $1 < j < k$ with $a_1 \cdots a_j = 2(r+1)$, $a_1 \cdots a_k = 2(N - r)$, $a_j > 2$ and $a_{j+1} > 2$. Let $\lambda$ consist of the parts of $P(a_1, \dots, a_j)$ together…
nodes.title: Halved perfect partitions are double-perfect but not of Type A

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$, $n \ge 2(r+1)$, and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$ whose largest part $\ell$ is not $r + 1$. Then $\lambda$ with one more part $\ell$ is a double-perfect partition of $n + \ell$ of order $r$. The condition $\ell \ne r + 1$ cannot be dropped: $(1^2, 3^4, 6)$ is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $20$ of order $5$, but $(1^2, 3^4, 6^2)$ is not a double-perfect…
nodes.title: Adding a copy of the largest part to a double-perfect partition

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$, $n \ge 2(r+1)$, and let $\lambda$ be a double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$. For every $m \ge 0$, adding $m$ parts equal to $n - r$ to $\lambda$ gives a double-perfect partition of $n + m(n - r)$ of order $r$.
nodes.title: Inserting copies of a part into a double-perfect partition

nodes.summary: A double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ is a finite multiset $\lambda$ of positive integers with sum $N$ such that, for every integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le N$, the number of distinct sub-multisets of $\lambda$ with sum $m$ is $2$ if $r + 1 \le m \le N - r - 1$ and $1$ otherwise. Their set is denoted $U_r(N)$; order $1$ gives the double-perfect partitions.
nodes.title: Double-perfect partitions of higher order

nodes.summary: Let $N > 3$. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $1$ if and only if there is a perfect partition $\beta$ of $N - 2$ such that either $1$ occurs exactly once in $\beta$ and $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with two more parts equal to $1$, or $2$ is not a part of $\beta$ and $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with one more part equal to $2$.
nodes.title: Double-perfect partitions from perfect partitions

nodes.summary: The partition $(1^3, 4)$ of $7$, with three parts equal to $1$ and one part equal to $4$, is a perfect partition of $7$.
nodes.title: A perfect partition of seven

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a perfect partition of $n$ when its elements are positive, they sum to $n$, and for every integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ exactly one partition of $m$ is contained in $\lambda$, that is, exactly one sub-multiset of $\lambda$ has sum $m$ (equal sub-multisets are counted once).
nodes.title: Perfect partition

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2(r+1)$ be integers, and let $\lambda$ be a Type-A double-perfect partition of $n$ of order $r$. Then for every natural number $m$, the partition obtained from $\lambda$ by adding $m$ parts equal to $n - r$ is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $n + m(n - r)$ of order $r$.
nodes.title: Adding equal parts to a Type-A double-perfect partition

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 2(r+1)$ be integers. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ if and only if there is a perfect partition $\beta$ of $N - r - 1$ such that either $1$ occurs exactly $r$ times in $\beta$ and $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with $r + 1$ parts equal to $1$ added, or $1$ does not occur exactly $r$ times in $\beta$, $r + 1$ is not a part of $\beta$,…
nodes.title: Characterization of Type-A double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: The partition $(1^5, 2)$ of $7$, with five parts equal to $1$ and one part equal to $2$, is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $7$ of order $1$.
nodes.title: A Type-A double-perfect partition of seven

nodes.summary: Let $r$ and $N$ be natural numbers. A multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers is a Type-A double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ when $\lambda$ is a double-perfect partition of $N$ of order $r$ and there is a perfect partition $\beta$ of $N - r - 1$ (read as $0$ when $N \le r$) such that $\lambda$ is $\beta$ with $r + 1$ parts equal to $1$ added, or $\beta$ with one part equal to $r + 1$ added. The set of these…
nodes.title: Type-A double-perfect partition

nodes.summary: Let $f_k(n)$ be the truncated recursion with $f_0(n) = 0$, $f_{k+1}(1) = 1$, and $f_{k+1}(n)$ the sum of $f_k(d)$ over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$ when $n \ne 1$. For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $n \le k$, $f_k(n) = f(n)$, where $f(n)$ is the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$.
nodes.title: The truncated ordered-factorization recursion stabilizes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, define $f_k(n)$ by recursion on $k$: $f_0(n) = 0$, $f_{k+1}(1) = 1$, and for $n \ne 1$, $f_{k+1}(n)$ is the sum of $f_k(d)$ over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$, that is, the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $1 \le d < n$ (there are none when $n = 0$).
nodes.title: Truncated recursion for ordered factorizations

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 2$, the number $f(n)$ of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$ satisfies $f(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\ d < n} f(d)$, the sum running over the proper divisors $d$ of $n$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the number of ordered factorizations

nodes.summary: The number $f(n)$ of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$ takes the values $f(0) = 0$, $f(1) = 1$, $f(6) = 3$ and $f(12) = 8$.
nodes.title: Small values of the ordered factorization count

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 2$, $f(n)$ is the number of ordered factorizations $n = a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$ of $n$ into factors $a_i > 1$ (OEIS A074206); moreover $f(0) = 0$ and $f(1) = 1$.
nodes.title: Number of ordered factorizations

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 0$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_k \ge 1$ be integers. The parts of the partition $(1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, (a_1a_2)^{a_3-1}, \dots, (a_1\cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$ that MacMahon's bijection attaches to the ordered factorization $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$, where $x^e$ denotes $e$ parts equal to $x$, sum to $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k - 1$.
nodes.title: The partition of a factorization sums to the product minus one

nodes.summary: MacMahon's bijection sends the ordered factorization $6 = 2 \cdot 3$ to the partition $(1, 2^2) = (1, 2, 2)$ of $5$.
nodes.title: MacMahon's partition of the factorization 2 · 3

nodes.summary: To a finite sequence $(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ of natural numbers, read as the ordered factorization $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k$, attach the multiset of parts $(1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, (a_1a_2)^{a_3-1}, \dots, (a_1\cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$, where $x^e$ denotes $e$ parts equal to $x$ and an exponent $a_i - 1$ is read as $0$ when $a_i = 0$. In particular the empty sequence gives the empty multiset.
nodes.title: MacMahon's partition of an ordered factorization

nodes.summary: For a multiset $\lambda$ of natural numbers and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of partitions of $m$ contained in $\lambda$ is the number of distinct sub-multisets of $\lambda$ whose elements sum to $m$.
nodes.title: Number of subpartitions with a given sum

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 2(r+1)$. For a finite sequence $(a_1, \dots, a_k)$ write $P(a_1, \dots, a_k) = (1^{a_1-1}, a_1^{a_2-1}, \dots, (a_1\cdots a_{k-1})^{a_k-1})$ for the partition that MacMahon's bijection attaches to the ordered factorization $a_1 \cdots a_k$, where $x^e$ denotes $e$ parts equal to $x$, and let $\cup$ join parts with multiplicity. nodes.title: Shapes of Type-A double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$. Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 2(r+1)$, that is, $1 \le r \le \lfloor (N-2)/2 \rfloor$, and put $M = 2(r+1)$. The number $d_r(N)$ of Type-A double-perfect partitions of $N$ of order $r$ is $f(N-r) - f((N-r)/M) - (f(r+1) - 1) f((N-r)/(r+1))$ if $N \equiv r \pmod M$, $f(N-r) - (f(r+1) - 1) f((N-r)/(r+1))$ if $N \equiv -1 \pmod M$, and…
nodes.title: Number of Type-A double-perfect partitions

nodes.summary: Let $f(n)$ be the number of ordered factorizations of $n$ into factors greater than $1$. Let $r \ge 1$ and $N \ge 3r + 4$, that is, $1 \le r \le \lfloor (N-4)/3 \rfloor$, and put $M = 2(r+1)$ and $c = f(M) - 1 - f(r+1)$. nodes.title: Number of Type-B double-perfect partitions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
